passage:
A museum workshop taught students how ancient ink was made from soot, water, and natural glue. Students ground materials slowly and tested the ink with brushes.
The process took patience. Modern pens suddenly seemed miraculous.
The guide explained that writing materials shaped what people wrote and how long records lasted. Ink, paper, and climate all affected history.
Students wrote their names with the handmade ink and waited for it to dry.
They learned that writing is not only language. It is chemistry, tools, time, and surface.
Every message depends on materials. Without them, thoughts cannot travel far.
